title: Adaptive reservation intake: predictive demand scoring, auto-approval thresholds, and capacity hedging
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers submit reservation requests for dedicated capacity with wide variance in projected consumption and time-to-use. The current manual approval flow causes long lead times for low-risk requests and inconsistent capacity hedging that increases cost or results in late provisioning.

This ticket proposes an Adaptive Reservation Intake workflow that combines a predictive demand scoring model, auto-approval gates for low-risk requests, and explicit capacity hedging suggestions for higher-uncertainty requests. The goal is to reduce mean approval time for low-friction reservations by >= 70%, improve utilization of reserved pools, and reduce emergency provisioning incidents by automating evidence-backed decisioning while keeping ops and finance control knobs intact.
background: Existing reservation playbooks (see related PM docs in product-management) rely on manual reviewers and static SLA windows. We have telemetry (usage history, customer-run rates, burst patterns) and a draft forecasting model from Research (model-score-forecast-v0). There is no standard UI representation of uncertainty or a consistent auto-approval policy tied to a probabilistic risk score. Ops currently keeps a 20% global hedging buffer which is expensive and blunt.
proposal_summary:
1) Add a predictive demand score (0-100) for each intake that estimates probability of reaching the requested committed throughput within the requested onboarding window.
2) Define auto-approval thresholds (e.g., score >= 85% -> auto-approve; 60-85% -> auto-approve with hedging recommendation; <60% -> require manual review).
3) Introduce capacity hedging guidance: suggest a provisional reservation size (e.g., 70% of requested throughput) and a time-bound provisional credit that converts to full reservation after validated consumption.
4) Expose a Simulator in Console to run probabilistic usage scenarios and show expected utilization, cost delta, and risk of shortage.
5) Add audit trail entries and escalation hooks for Finance/Ops to override auto-approval rules.
user_stories: As a Platform PM, I want low-risk requests auto-approved so my team can focus on high-risk provisioning and lifecycle management.
As an Engineering lead, I want hedging suggestions so we can avoid over-provisioning while meeting customer SLAs.
As an Ops reviewer, I want a simulator showing probability bands so I can approve or adjust reservations with evidence.
As a Customer, I want faster provisioning for standard requests and transparent guidance when we are given provisional capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive demand score surfaces on every reservation intake (API + Console) and matches production model outputs within 5% of test set validation.
Auto-approval pipeline approves >= 70% of existing 'low-friction' historical requests in the staging replay without manual intervention.
Console Simulator provides at least three scenario bands (optimistic, median, conservative) and a visualization of hedging recommendations.
Audit log entries created for every auto-approval with model version and score; ops overrides are recorded with reason.
No customer-facing SLA regressions in canary region for 30 days after rollout; monitor bump in emergency provisioning incidents and keep below baseline.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive auto-approval reduces lead time but increases risk of stranded capacity; hedging policy aims to mitigate by time-limited provisional reservations.
We considered a full commitment escrow model (bill now, activate later) but Finance prefers consumption-validated conversion to avoid invoicing complexity.
Model fairness: block auto-approval for enterprise customers flagged with special contractual terms until legal review; this is a ruleset in policy engine.
Initial hedging suggestion default: provisional_size = max(ceil(requested*0.7), min_unit) adjustable per account tier.
